explanation: The capital city of the kingdom of Judah, which was destroyed by the Babylonians under Nebuchadnezzar II.
King of Babylon, who conquered and destroyed Jerusalem and led the Jews into exile.
The condition of being forced to leave one's homeland and live in a foreign land, as the Jews experienced after the fall of Jerusalem.
The holy place in Jerusalem where the Jews performed their religious ceremonies and sacrifices. Destroyed by the Babylonians.
The last king of Judah, who was captured by Nebuchadnezzar and taken to Babylon.
An ancient city and empire in Mesopotamia, known for its power and cultural influence. The place where the Jews were led into exile.
Former king of Judah, who also was captured by Nebuchadnezzar and taken to Babylon.
Son of Nebuchadnezzar and king of Babylon, who released Jehoiachin from captivity and treated him with respect.
